dedupe_keys.name: us railroad climate hazard exposure database floods heat and landslides 2000 to 2024

description: This database assigns historical natural hazard events to segments of the US railroad network: riverine floods and flash floods through HUC-12 watersheds, heat and excessive heat through National Weather Service forecast zones from the NCEI Storm Events Database, and landslides from USGS point and polygon inventories within a buffer of the track. Each segment carries event identifiers, hazard type, event counts and frequencies (for example flash flood, flood and heat frequency) and its length, with Federal Railroad Administration accident records used only to verify that up to half of hazard-linked accidents fall on the date of a recorded event. It was built by Benyamin Ghoreishi and colleagues at Oregon State and Clemson universities and described in Scientific Data (12:1932, December 2025). Coverage is national for the continental United States at segment level from 2000 to 2024. The data are free on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 (v1.1.0, an 11 GB data archive with shapefile, GeoPackage and CSV layers, plus the Python scripts), with code on GitHub. Caveats: assignments show potential exposure by proximity or zone, not verified damage, and heat is assigned by forecast zone. The data support hazard exposure, fragility and resilience studies and climate adaptation planning of rail freight networks, alongside accident records and network flow models.
